staticText: Cholera Urgency and Outbreak Checklist for /tools/cholera-risk/. Explain only the deterministic non-diagnostic escalation hierarchy. Shock signs or inability to drink safely require emergency rehydration-capable care now. Very frequent watery stools, repeated vomiting, dehydration signs or blood in stool require urgent medical assessment. Acute watery diarrhoea in a higher-risk person or outbreak context requires same-day care and official local public-health guidance. Packaged oral rehydration solution may be mentioned only for a person who is awake and able to drink, exactly as the label or a health worker directs, without delaying travel. Do not diagnose or rule out cholera, provide antibiotics, doses or a personalised home-mixing/treatment recipe, delay care, or claim real-time outbreak status. Symptoms and exposure are sensitive and local: do not request identifiers or exact location, and do not store, log, upload, sync, email, add selections to URLs or send them to analytics. Sources reviewed 2026-07-26: WHO Cholera fact sheet and WHO Cholera Outbreaks questions and answers.
